content: 4-Methylbenzylidene camphor, commonly abbreviated as 4-MBC, is an organic derivative of camphor. It is also known by its chemical names 3-(4-Methylbenzylidene)bornan-2-one or 3-(4-Methylbenzylidene)-dl-camphor. This compound is utilized in the cosmetic industry due to its ability to protect the skin from ultraviolet (UV) radiation, particularly UVB rays. As a result, it is a common ingredient in sunscreen lotions and deodorants. Its commercial trade name is Eusolex® 6300. Studies have raised concerns about 4-MBC acting as an endocrine disruptor. There is ongoing debate regarding its estrogenic effects. While one study reported only minor estrogenic activity, another study conducted in Switzerland demonstrated significant uterine growth in immature rodents exposed to 4-MBC. Furthermore, there is evidence suggesting that 4-MBC may suppress the pituitary-thyroid axis, potentially leading to hypothyroidism. Additionally, this compound has been associated with the development of photoallergic dermatitis in some individuals. Regarding its regulatory status, 4-MBC is approved for use in Europe by the European Union's Scientific Committee for Cosmetic Products and Non-Food Products. It is also approved for use in Canada by Health Canada, as well as in Australia and several other countries. However, it is not approved for use in the United States by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and is prohibited in Japan.
